title: Finite evaluation of canonical whole-system regular multiplication
statement: For a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, a scheme morphism f:X to Y, reductions rX and rY of [def-pur-completed-unit-pullback-data], and n a natural number, evaluation of systemMultiplication followed by rX.finite equals inverseEvaluation.hom followed by pullback of rY.finite and finiteMultiplication. All arrows are those fixed by the actual coefficient ring maps and adjunctions in [lem-pur-completed-primitive-counit-comparison].

source.place: Sections 3.5 and 6.5, Lemmas 6.5.9 and 6.8.2; regular-module calculation in lem-pur-completed-unit-pullback-tower

proof.text: Cancel inverseEvaluation on the source and transpose under the finite adjunction. A generic adjunction-mate calculation uses its normalized unit equation and naturality of the direct-evaluation isomorphism. Finite Hom-equivalence naturality reduces to the ring arrows. On each section, the equality-transport map is the identity up to HEq; rX.finite_sections and rY.finite_sections remove the two finite identifications. Equality induction for the two ring-section transports identifies ringComponent with the finite constant-section ring map. The transposes agree, and injectivity of the Hom equivalence gives the original equation.

lean.statement:
theorem completedUnitMultiplicationComponents {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (rX : Reduction l E X (calculus l E X))
    (rY : Reduction l E Y (calculus l E Y)) (n : ℕ) :
    (coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E X n).map (systemMultiplication l E f) ≫
        (rX.finite n).hom =
      (PrimitiveCounit.inverseEvaluation l E f n).hom.app (systemUnit l E Y) ≫
        (integralOperationsLevelPullback l E f n).map (rY.finite n).hom ≫
          finiteMultiplication l E f n
